Science Doctoral Scholarships
NB: Please see the 'UC Doctoral Scholarships' webpage for more information on our centrally-funded group of scholarships.
The following doctoral scholarship opportunities are funded by either external organisations, grants, donations and bequests to the university. Discover some of the other scholarships that may assist in funding your Engineering or Forestry doctoral degree below.
Each scholarship has different other eligibility criteria so click on the scholarship name and then click through to the Regulations link to determine if you're eligible.
PLEASE NOTE THAT THIS INFORMATION MAY BE SUBJECT TO CHANGE: These scholarships are subject to funding availability and are reviewed each year.
Search our scholarships database for all scholarships currently available.
Engineering
Canterbury Chemeca Trust Fund
Purpose: To support participation in conferences, workshops, and events of a similar kind in Australasia by students and staff of the Department of Chemical and Process Engineering at UC.
Value: Financial assistance according to funds available. No grant will usually exceed $1,000
Closing date: 30 June - Applications should be made directly to the Department of Chemical and Process Engineering
Coastal and Ocean Engineering Conference Fund
Purpose: To support research students at UC to present papers at coastal and/or ocean conferences (normally those in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand). Applicants must be enrolled in a research programme in the Department of Civil & Natural Resources Engineering or Geography.
Value: Varies - individual grants do not normally exceed the following values: (a) For conferences in Aotearoa New Zealand: $1,000; (b) For conferences in Australia: $1,500; (c) For conferences in other countries: $3,000.
Closing date: 31 March and 30 September if funds available
Dick & Mary Earle Scholarship in Technology
Purpose: To support and encourage postgraduate research into one or both of these fields: (a) innovation and product development; or (b) bioprocess technology. NB: this is a Universities NZ scholarship.
Value: Financial assistance up to a value of $17,000 per annum for up to 2 years (Masters) or $25,000 per annum for up to 3 years (Doctoral).
Closing date: 01 July
Electric Power Engineering Centre (EPECentre) Postgraduate Scholarship (Postgrad)
Purpose: To recognise academic achievement by postgraduate students at UC who are specialising in Electric Power Engineering.
Value: Financial assistance of up to a value of: $12,500 for one year (for Master of Engineering students); or $25,000 per annum for up to three years (for PhD students).
Closing date: Applications can be submitted any time. Applications must be submitted in writing to the Director of the Electric Power Engineering Centre (EPECentre).
G B Battersby-Trimble Scholarship in Computer Science
Purpose: To support students studying Computer Science at UC. Applicants must be enrolled in either (a) the final year of an honours degree in Computer Science; (b) a Master's degree in Computer Science; or (c) a PhD in Computer Science.
Value: Financial assistance for one year to the value of: (a) $2,000 for honours or masters students doing courses; (b) $7,000 for master's thesis students; or (c) $8,000 for PhD thesis students.
Closing date: 31 March
east
Nick - UC Computer Science doctoral student
I never imagined I’d return to academia, let alone proceed with postgraduate studies. Giving up career development and a steady income for such a period is a very difficult decision. However, I can already see that developing trends will make coding skills compulsory, regardless of industry.
Financial support, especially during such a lengthy endeavour, is invaluable. It means spending less time reading bank statements, fewer working hours, and more time in the labs. The recognition and acknowledgement are highly motivating, especially for isolated undertakings such as scientific research.
Overall, receiving a scholarship has provided much-needed financial and emotional support for me to complete my PhD. I wish take the chance to thank my supervisors who assisted me in the successful application.
2025 G B Battersby-Trimble Scholarship in Computer Science
2020 UC Mathematics and Statistics Scholarship
Henry Kelsey Scholarship
Purpose: To provide financial assistance to a student undertaking postgraduate research towards a Masters or Doctoral degree at a New Zealand university or research institution, studying muscular function, including - but not limited to - the causes and treatment of muscular dysfunction. NB: This is a Universities New Zealand Scholarship
Value: Financial assistance up to $15,000 per annum for up to two years for Master's study or three years for Doctoral study.
Closing date: 01 October
Keith Laugesen Scholarship
Purpose: To provide financial support for full-time PhD students studying in the Engineering and Science fields at UC.
Value: Financial assistance at a value of $24,500 per 120 points of enrolment; for up to a total of 360 points
Closing date: 31 October - there may only be one holder at a time so the scholarship is available approximately every third year.
Mechanical Engineering Crispin Hales Awhi Pūtea | Financial Need Grant
Purpose: To provide manaakitanga | support to Mechanical Engineering students who are experiencing financial difficulties.
Value: Financial assistance up to $1,000 for one year.
Closing date: Made available as funds permit -Applications must be made to the Mechanical Engineering Pastoral Care Office via mechanicalengineering@canterbury.ac.nz
Ngau Boon Keat Postgraduate Scholarship in Mechanical Engineering
Purpose: To support students enrolled in the Department of Mechanical Engineering either in a Master of Engineering degree, a Master of Engineering Studies degree, or a doctoral degree.
Value: Financial assistance up to a value of $25,000 per annum for up to 120 points of enrolment (Master's students) or 360 points of enrolment (PhD students).
Closing date: 31 October
Pukehou Poutu Scholarship
Purpose: To support postgraduate study in either agricultural or silvicultural science. NB: This is a Universities New Zealand Scholarship.
Value: Financial assistance up to a value of $10,000 for one year.
Closing date: 01 October
Roger Helm Scholarship in Pure Mathematics
Purpose: To support full-time students for study towards a research master’s degree or a PhD degree in Pure Mathematics at UC.
Value: Financial assistance at a value of $5,000 for one year.
Closing date: 31 October
Tait Communications Doctoral Research Scholarship
Purpose: To encourage Doctoral research related to Critical Information and Communications Technology (CICT) at UC. The proposed research must be of relevance to the current interests of Tait Communications. Preference will be given to applicants undertaking relevant research in conjunction with the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering including the Wireless Research Centre at the University.
Value: Financial assistance up to a value of $35,000 per annum for up to 3 years.
Closing date: 31 October - only one holder of the scholarship is possible at any one time so scholarship advertised when available.
UC Engineering PhD Publishing Scholarship
Purpose: To support PhD thesis candidates who have submitted their thesis for examination having studied in the Faculty of Engineering at UC so they can prepare and submit papers for publication in peer-reviewed journals of international standing. The aim is to support a Faculty of Engineering increase in world and PBRF rankings.
Value: Financial assistance of $3,750 for 3 months.
Closing date: Applications can be submitted Applications must be made to the Faculty of Engineering at any time - Scholarships will be made available as funds become available.
Wal McQuarrie Memorial Scholarship
Purpose: To support research by students studying full-time in a Master of Civil Engineering (MCivilEng) degree (or PhD in Civil Engineering) at UC.
Value: Financial assistance at a value of $8,000 for up to 120 points (or 360 points for PhD student).
Closing date: 31 October
east
Forestry
McKelvey Award
Purpose: To support master’s and PhD students in Te Kura Ngahere | School of Forestry at UC, by contributing to expenses associated with presenting a paper at a relevant conference. In the absence of suitable candidates, the applications may be opened to eligible students seeking support to meet other costs associated with their study.
Value: Financial assistance up the to value of $1,000.
Closing date: 01 April and 31 October (if the available fund has not been allocated in the 01 April round)
Owen Browning Scholarship in Forestry
Purpose: To support full-time postgraduate students studying Forestry or Forest Engineering at UC. Specific eligiblity criteria applies, check Regulations for details.
Value: Financial assistance up to a value of $4,500 per annum; for up to 120 points of enrolment (Masters) or 240 points of enrolment (PhD).
Closing date: 31 October
Pukehou Poutu Scholarship
Purpose: To support postgraduate study in either agricultural or silvicultural science. NB: This is a Universities New Zealand Scholarship.
Value: Financial assistance up to a value of $10,000 for one year.
Closing date: 01 October
TW Adams Scholarship in Forestry
Purpose: To promote MForSc and PhD studies in Te Kura Ngahere | School of Forestry at UC.
Value: Financial assistance of up to $9,000 for 120 points for MForSc students; or $15,000 pa for up to 240 points of enrolment for PhD students.
Closing date: 31 October
UC Engineering PhD Publishing Scholarship
Purpose: To support PhD thesis candidates who have submitted their thesis for examination having studied in the Faculty of Engineering at UC so they can prepare and submit papers for publication in peer-reviewed journals of international standing. The aim is to support a Faculty of Engineering increase in world and PBRF rankings.
Value: Financial assistance of $3,750 for 3 months.
Closing date: Applications can be submitted Applications must be made to the Faculty of Engineering at any time - Scholarships will be made available as funds become available.
east
Also visit the School of Forestry scholarships wepage for details on some other externally funded opportunities.
Joseph - UC Forestry doctoral student
Receiving the UC Forestry Research Support Scholarship and the TW Adams Scholarship in Forestry has provided myself with valuable support throughout my PhD research.
These scholarships have reduced the financial pressures associated with postgraduate study, allowing me to focus more time on my research.
My PhD explores the use of remote sensing technologies to map and classify tree species within plantation forests across New Zealand through the combination of satellite imagery and drone-based data.
The support provided by these scholarships has enabled me to dedicate more time to fieldwork, data processing, analysis, and the development of new methodologies for the application of remote sensing in forestry.
Beyond financial assistance, these scholarships represent an investment within forestry research and innovation for which I am grateful for the opportunity to contribute to. This research has the potential to improve forest management and decision-making.
2025 T W Adams Scholarship in Forestry
2025 UC Forestry Research Support Scholarship
2024 UC Forestry PhD Scholarship
